description: Two window-stage gaps found together. (1) ANY registered aggregate is usable as a window function over the frame - ARRAY_AGG(x) OVER (PARTITION BY g), LISTAGG, MEDIAN and the rest - where only a hard-coded set (SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX/COUNT) used to be dispatched and everything else threw 'Unsupported window function'. (2) A GROUPED query with a window function: after GROUP BY the rows are already SELECT-list-shaped, so the window stage must resolve names against the PROJECTED columns - a window's ORDER BY commonly references an aggregate's ALIAS - and take non-window values POSITIONALLY. Re-evaluating each item against the BASE table sent aggregate text to the scalar evaluator, giving 'Unknown function: ARRAY_AGG'. QUALIFY over such a grouped window rank must filter it. Converted 1:1 from query/AggregateAsWindowFunctionTest (now retired); the Java read individual row indexes out of a ResultSet, which the converted tests state as whole ordered row sets.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t (g INTEGER, v VARCHAR, m INTEGER)
SELECT g, ARRAY_AGG(v) OVER (PARTITION BY g) FROM t WHERE g = 2

skip.reason: asserts the exact element ORDER of ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT ...) without a WITHIN GROUP clause; the order of a distinct aggregation is unspecified, so a real account may build the array in any order.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t (g INTEGER, v VARCHAR, m INTEGER)
SELECT DISTINCT g, ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT v) OVER (PARTITION BY g) AS vs FROM t ORDER BY g
CREATE TABLE t (g INTEGER, v VARCHAR, m INTEGER)
SELECT LISTAGG(v) OVER (PARTITION BY g) FROM t WHERE g = 2
SELECT MEDIAN(m) OVER (PARTITION BY g) FROM t WHERE g = 2
CREATE TABLE t (g INTEGER, v VARCHAR, m INTEGER)
SELECT g, SUM(m) AS metric, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY metric DESC) AS rnk FROM t GROUP BY g, v ORDER BY g, rnk
CREATE TABLE t (g INTEGER, v VARCHAR, m INTEGER)
SELECT g, ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT v) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY v) AS vals, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY g) AS rnk FROM t GROUP BY g ORDER BY g
CREATE TABLE t (g INTEGER, v VARCHAR, m INTEGER)
SELECT g, SUM(m) AS metric, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY metric DESC) AS rnk FROM t GROUP BY g, v QUALIFY rnk = 1 ORDER BY g
CREATE TABLE t (g INTEGER, v VARCHAR, m INTEGER)
SELECT g, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY m) FROM t
SELECT g, SUM(m) FROM t GROUP BY g
